label: copy-phase input k (fed-back k)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the input token is k (the model feeding its own previously output k back in). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, nor on any other input token; every dev activation satisfies the predicate (recall 1.0). About 27% of copy-phase k inputs stay silent, mostly early in the copy phase: recall_idx 0 never fires and the firing rate rises with recall_idx and t. Magnitude is largest when the k is fed back late in a long sequence (the top examples are mostly the final copy step, to_go 0, t around 14-17) and smallest when k is recalled at positions 1-2. The output token (what is being recalled now) has almost no effect.

issues: All the factual claims hold on dev. 100% of the activation mass is in the copy phase and every activation is on in_tok=k. There are zero activations in the original or delimiter phases and zero at recall_idx 0. Top examples are mostly to_go 0 (precision there is 0.87).
Test misses: only 2 missed activations (0.0% of the mass, scattered). There are 24,050 false positives, i.e. copy-phase k inputs where the feature stays silent.
The silent cases depend on position in a graded way, not as a sharp boundary. Precision by recall_idx is 0.44 at 1, 0.66 at 2, 0.76 at 3 and 0.87 at 4 or more.

The explanation leaves out a strong dependence on sequence length L. Precision by L is 0.05 at L=3, 0.44 at L=4, 0.63 at L=5, 0.70 at L=6 and 0.84 at L=9. At recall_idx 1, precision is 0.06 for L<=5 but 0.81 for L>=8. So 'silent mostly early in the copy phase' is really 'silent in short sequences and early in the copy phase'. This rises smoothly and looks like a magnitude threshold effect, not a separate class.

Adding position or length conditions improves the predicate only slightly. '(phase==2)&(in_tok==k)&((L>=6)|(recall_idx>=3))' scores test F1 0.864 and '...&(L>=5)&(t>=7)' scores 0.864, against 0.848 for the original. Because the gain is this small, keeping the simpler predicate is a fair choice.
Even at L=9, about 16% of late-position k inputs stay silent, and the rendered false positives show no visible token or history pattern. I am treating this as noise in the low-activation tail.
